rubric_version.description: The rubric version in force when this judgment was made. `replay` compares it against the rubric on disk and refuses on a mismatch, so a threshold change cannot silently re-decide a past verdict.

rubric_hash.description: Hash of the complete effective rubric content used to route this result.

source_rubric_version.description: Rubric version under which the saved model answers were originally collected.

source_rubric_hash.description: Rubric content hash under which the saved model answers were originally collected; null for legacy results.

runtime.description: The build that produced this result. The two runtimes must agree on every other field; this is the one they are supposed to differ on.

confidence.description: Certainty of the answers that produced this verdict: the minimum over deciding_answers. 0 when no rule-bound answer decided it. This is not a probability that the verdict is correct.

confidence_floor.description: The floor an automatic pass/fail had to clear, from the rubric's confidence_floors[stakes].

deciding_answers.description: Answer IDs the matched rule read. Only these contribute to confidence.

model.description: The model that answered, as the API reported it — not necessarily the model the rubric asked for, since the API may resolve an alias. Under --mock nothing answers, so it is the requested model (jev-1.13.0).

requested_model.description: The version pinned by the rubric before provider alias resolution.

state_projection.description: Allowlisted state_filter paths and the top-level keys that survived filtering.

paths.description: Sorted path strings from the rubric state_filter.

hash.description: Stable sha256 hash of the sorted paths list.

projected_keys.description: Top-level keys present in the filtered state sent to Jev.

deterministic_gates.description: Outcomes of deterministic checks run in code (not Jev). Always present.

usage.description: Token counts. Both fields are always present and are null when the API reported none, so a result has one shape whichever runtime produced it.
